translations.idiomatic: Who could have imagined that he would prove utterly wicked and extreme in perversity — from childhood on, as he grew he shunned no evil however small and rushed into every great evil without fail.

sentences.zh: 前後訓誘，常加隱蔽，險戾難移，日月滋甚。

translations.literal: Instruction and admonition before and after were constantly concealed from him; his fierce perversity could not be moved, and day by day it grew worse.
translations.idiomatic: Instruction and admonition were constantly offered yet constantly concealed from him; his fierce perversity could not be moved, and day by day it grew worse.

sentences.zh: 棄冠毀冕，長襲戎衣，犬馬是狎，鷹隼是愛，皁歷軒殿之中，韝緤宸扆之側。

translations.literal: He cast aside cap and robes, long wearing martial dress; dogs and horses were his intimates, hawks and falcons his delight; black caps entered the halls of the palace, hawking gloves hung at the side of the imperial screen.
translations.idiomatic: He cast aside cap and robes and long wore martial dress; dogs and horses were his intimates, hawks and falcons his delight; common caps entered the palace halls, and hawking gloves hung at the side of the imperial screen.

sentences.zh: 至乃單騎遠郊，獨宿深野，手揮矛鋋，躬行刳斮，白刃為弄器，斬害為恒務。

translations.literal: He would even ride alone far into the suburbs, lodge alone in deep wilds, wave spear and trident, and himself perform dismemberments; bare blades were his playthings, and cutting down and killing his constant occupation.
translations.idiomatic: He would even ride alone far into the suburbs and lodge alone in deep wilds, waving spear and trident while himself performing dismemberments; bare blades were his playthings, and killing his constant occupation.

sentences.zh: 捨交戟之衞，委天畢之儀，趨步闤闠，酣歌壚肆，宵遊忘反，宴寢營舍，奪人子女，掠人財物，方筴所不書，振古所未聞。

translations.literal: He abandoned the crossed-halberd guard and cast off the heavenly-weapon ritual, hastening through market wards, singing drunk in wine shops; night excursions forgot return, feasts and sleeping in barrack quarters; he seized people's sons and daughters and plundered people's goods — what the regional gazetteers do not record, what in all antiquity was never heard.
translations.idiomatic: He abandoned the crossed-halberd guard and cast off the heavenly-weapon ritual, hurrying through market wards and singing drunk in wine shops; on night excursions he forgot to return, feasting and sleeping in barrack quarters; he seized people's sons and daughters and plundered their goods — things the regional gazetteers do not record and antiquity has never heard.

sentences.zh: 沈勃儒士，孫超功臣，幼文兄弟，並豫勳効，四人無罪，一朝同戮。

translations.literal: Shen Bo was a Confucian scholar; Sun Chao a meritorious minister; the brothers Du Youwen all shared in the dynasty's achievement — the four men were without guilt, yet in one morning were slain together.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Bo was a Confucian scholar; Sun Chao a meritorious minister; the brothers Du Youwen all shared in the dynasty's achievement — all four were guiltless, yet in one morning they were slain together.

sentences.zh: 飛鏃鼓劍，孩稚無遺，屠裂肝腸，以為戲謔，投骸江流，以為歡笑。

translations.literal: He shot arrows and beat swords; infants were left none; he tore open livers and intestines as jest, cast corpses into the river current for amusement.
translations.idiomatic: He shot arrows and beat swords; not an infant was spared; he tore open livers and intestines for sport and cast corpses into the river for amusement.

sentences.zh: 又淫費無度，帑藏空竭，橫賦關河，專充別蓄，黔庶嗷嗷，厝生無所。

translations.literal: Moreover he squandered without limit; the treasury was emptied; he imposed levies across the passes and rivers solely to fill separate stores, while the common people wailed and found no place to set their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover he squandered without limit until the treasury stood empty; he imposed levies across the passes and rivers solely to fill separate stores, while the common people wailed and had nowhere to set their lives.

sentences.zh: 吾與其所生每厲以義方，遂謀酖毒，將騁凶忿。

translations.literal: I, together with his birth mother, constantly admonished him with the righteous way; then he plotted poison, intending to unleash his fierce hatred.
translations.idiomatic: I, together with his birth mother, constantly admonished him in the righteous way; then he plotted poison, intending to unleash his fierce hatred.

sentences.zh: 沈憂假日，慮不終朝。

translations.literal: Deep sorrow filled borrowed days; dread that the end would not reach the morrow.
translations.idiomatic: Deep sorrow filled my borrowed days; I dreaded that the end would not reach the morrow.

sentences.zh: 自昔辛、癸，爰及幽、厲，方之於此，未譬萬分。

translations.literal: From Xin and Gui of old down to You and Li, compared with this he is not one ten-thousandth.
translations.idiomatic: From Xin and Gui of old down to You and Li — compared with this, he is not one part in ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 民怨既深，神怒已積，七廟阽危，四海褫氣。

translations.literal: The people's resentment has deepened; the spirits' wrath has accumulated; the seven temples teeter on the brink, and the four seas have lost their breath.
translations.idiomatic: The people's resentment has deepened; the spirits' wrath has accumulated; the seven temples teeter on the brink, and the four seas have lost their breath.

sentences.zh: 廢昏立明，前代令範，況迺滅義反道，天人所棄，釁深牧野，理絕桐宮。

translations.literal: Deposing the dark and establishing the bright is the proper model of former ages; how much more when he has extinguished righteousness and reversed the Way — abandoned by Heaven and man, his guilt as deep as Muye, his principle as severed as Tong Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Deposing the dark and establishing the bright is the proper model of former ages; how much more when he has extinguished righteousness and reversed the Way — abandoned by Heaven and man, his guilt as deep as at Muye, his principle as severed as at Tong Palace.

sentences.zh: 故密令蕭領軍潛運明略，幽顯協規，普天同泰。

translations.literal: Therefore I have secretly ordered General Xiao of the Guards to set in motion a clear plan in secret, with the hidden and manifest joining in counsel, and all under Heaven sharing peace.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I have secretly ordered General Xiao of the Guards to set a clear plan in motion, with the hidden and manifest joining in counsel so that all under Heaven may share peace.

sentences.zh: 驃騎大將軍安成王體自太宗，天挺淹叡，風神凝遠，德映在田。

translations.literal: The Prince of Ancheng, General of Agile Cavalry, is of the Taizong line himself; by Heaven's endowment deep and wise, his spirit and bearing collected and far-reaching, virtue shining in the fields.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Ancheng, General of Agile Cavalry, is himself of the Taizong line; Heaven endowed him with depth and wisdom, his spirit and bearing collected and far-reaching, his virtue shining even in the fields.

sentences.zh: 地隆親茂，皇曆攸歸，億兆係心，含生屬望。

translations.literal: His territory is lofty and his kinship thick; the imperial succession is his due; the hundred millions bind their hearts to him, and all living beings look to him.
translations.idiomatic: His territory is lofty and his kinship thick; the imperial succession is his due; the hundred millions bind their hearts to him, and all living beings look to him.

sentences.zh: 宜光奉祖宗，臨享萬國。

translations.literal: He should brightly serve the ancestors and face and enjoy the myriad states.
translations.idiomatic: He should brightly serve the ancestors and preside over the myriad states.

sentences.zh: 便依舊典，以時奉行。

translations.literal: Let him follow the old statutes and carry them out at the proper season.
translations.idiomatic: Let him follow the old statutes and carry them out at the proper season.

sentences.zh: 未亡人追往傷懷，永言感絕。

translations.literal: The surviving consort looks back in wounded grief and forever feels cut off in feeling.
translations.idiomatic: The surviving consort looks back in wounded grief and forever feels cut off in her heart.

sentences.zh: 太后又令曰：「昱窮凶極暴，自取灰滅，雖曰罪招，能無傷悼。

translations.literal: The empress dowager issued another decree: 「Yu was utterly wicked and extreme in violence and brought ruin on himself — though his guilt invites punishment, how can one not mourn?」
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager issued another decree: 「Yu was utterly wicked and extreme in violence and brought ruin on himself — though his guilt invites punishment, how can one not mourn?」

sentences.zh: 棄同品庶，顧所不忍。

translations.literal: Cast aside as one of the common ranks, yet I cannot bear it.
translations.idiomatic: To cast him aside as one of the common ranks is something I cannot bear.

sentences.zh: 可特追封蒼梧郡王。

translations.literal: He may specially be posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Cangwu.
translations.idiomatic: He may specially be posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Cangwu.

sentences.zh: 」葬丹陽秣陵縣郊壇西。

translations.literal: 」He was buried west of the suburban altar at Moling in Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: 」He was buried west of the suburban altar at Moling in Danyang.

sentences.zh: 初昱在東宮，年五六歲時，始就書學，而惰業好嬉戲，主帥不能禁。

translations.literal: Early when Yu was in the Eastern Palace, at five or six sui he first took up book learning, yet was idle in studies and fond of play; the chief tutor could not restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: Early when Yu was in the Eastern Palace, at five or six sui he first took up book learning, yet was idle in his studies and fond of play; the chief tutor could not restrain him.

sentences.zh: 好緣漆帳竿，去地丈餘，如此者半食久，乃下。

translations.literal: He liked climbing lacquered canopy poles a zhang and more above ground; only after half a meal's time would he come down.
translations.idiomatic: He liked climbing lacquered canopy poles more than a zhang above the ground and would come down only after half a meal's time.

sentences.zh: 年漸長，喜怒乖節，左右有失旨者，輒手加撲打。

translations.literal: As he gradually grew older, joy and anger lost all measure; when attendants to either side missed his intent he would at once lay on them with his hands.
translations.idiomatic: As he gradually grew older, joy and anger lost all measure; when attendants on either side missed his intent he would at once beat them with his hands.

sentences.zh: 徒跣蹲踞，以此為常。

translations.literal: Barefoot, crouching and squatting — this was his constant way.
translations.idiomatic: Going barefoot, crouching and squatting — this was his constant way.

sentences.zh: 主帥以白太宗，上輒敕昱所生，嚴加捶訓。

translations.literal: The chief tutor reported this to Taizong; the emperor would then order Yu's birth mother to beat and discipline him severely.
translations.idiomatic: The chief tutor reported this to Taizong; the emperor would then order Yu's birth mother to beat and discipline him severely.

sentences.zh: 及嗣位，內畏太后，外憚諸大臣，猶未得肆志。

translations.literal: When he succeeded to the throne, inwardly he feared the empress dowager and outwardly dreaded the great ministers, and still had not been able to indulge his will.
translations.idiomatic: When he succeeded to the throne, inwardly he feared the empress dowager and outwardly dreaded the great ministers, and still could not indulge his will.

sentences.zh: 自加元服，變態轉興，內外稍無以制。

translations.literal: After he received the capping rites his conduct changed and surged; inwardly and outwardly there was gradually none to restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: After he received the capping rites his conduct changed and surged; gradually there was no one within or without who could restrain him.

sentences.zh: 三年秋冬間，便好出遊行，太妃每乘青篾車，隨相檢攝。

translations.literal: Between autumn and winter of the third year he began to love going out on excursions; the grand imperial consort each time rode in a green bamboo carriage and followed to keep him in check.
translations.idiomatic: Between autumn and winter of the third year he began to love going out on excursions; the grand imperial consort each time rode in a green bamboo carriage and followed to keep him in check.

sentences.zh: 昱漸自放恣，太妃不復能禁。

translations.literal: Yu little by little let himself go; the grand imperial consort could no longer restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu little by little let himself go; the grand imperial consort could no longer restrain him.

sentences.zh: 單將左右，棄部伍，或十里、二十里，或入市里，或往營署，日暮乃歸。

translations.literal: He led only his attendants, abandoning his unit — sometimes ten or twenty li, sometimes into markets and lanes, sometimes to barrack offices; only at dusk would he return.
translations.idiomatic: He led only his attendants, abandoning his unit — sometimes ten or twenty li, sometimes into markets and lanes, sometimes to barrack offices; only at dusk would he return.

sentences.zh: 四年春夏，此行彌數。

translations.literal: In spring and summer of the fourth year these outings became ever more frequent.
translations.idiomatic: In spring and summer of the fourth year these outings became ever more frequent.

sentences.zh: 自京城剋定，意志轉驕，於是無日不出。

translations.literal: Once the capital region was secured his will turned ever more arrogant — from then on there was not a day he did not go out.
translations.idiomatic: Once the capital region was secured his will turned ever more arrogant — from then on there was not a day he did not go out.

sentences.zh: 與左右人解僧智、張五兒恒相馳逐，夜出，開承明門，夕去晨反，晨出暮歸。

translations.literal: With his attendants Jie Sengzhi and Zhang Wu'er he constantly raced in pursuit; at night he opened the Chenming Gate — going out at evening and returning at dawn, going out at dawn and returning at evening.
translations.idiomatic: With his attendants Jie Sengzhi and Zhang Wu'er he constantly raced in pursuit; at night he opened the Chenming Gate — going out at evening and returning at dawn, going out at dawn and returning at evening.

sentences.zh: 從者並執鋋矛，行人男女，及犬馬牛驢，值無免者。

translations.literal: His followers all grasped spear-tridents; men and women among travelers, and oxen, horses, donkeys, and mules they met — none escaped.
translations.idiomatic: His followers all grasped spear-tridents; men and women among travelers, and oxen, horses, donkeys, and mules they met — none escaped.

sentences.zh: 民間擾懼，晝日不敢開門，道上行人殆絕。

translations.literal: The people were alarmed and afraid; by daylight they dared not open their doors, and travelers on the roads were nearly gone altogether.
translations.idiomatic: The people were alarmed and afraid; by daylight they dared not open their doors, and travelers on the roads nearly vanished altogether.

sentences.zh: 常著小袴褶，未嘗服衣冠。

translations.literal: He constantly wore short trousers and jacket and never donned cap and robes.
translations.idiomatic: He constantly wore short trousers and jacket and never donned cap and robes.

sentences.zh: 或有忤意，輒加以虐刑。

translations.literal: When anyone offended his intent he would at once add cruel punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When anyone offended his intent he would at once inflict cruel punishment.

sentences.zh: 有白棓數十枚，各有名號，鍼椎鑿鋸之徒，不離左右。

translations.literal: He had several dozen white clubs, each with its name; piercing awls, chisels, and saws were never far from his side.
translations.idiomatic: He had several dozen white clubs, each with its name; piercing awls, chisels, and saws were never far from his side.

sentences.zh: 嘗以鐵椎椎人陰破，左右人見之有斂眉者，昱大怒，令此人袒胛正立，以矛刺胛洞過。

translations.literal: Once he struck a man's genitals with an iron mallet until they were smashed; when someone nearby winced he flew into a great rage and ordered the man to bare his shoulder and stand straight while he pierced the shoulder through with a spear.
translations.idiomatic: Once he struck a man's genitals with an iron mallet until they were smashed; when someone nearby winced he flew into a great rage and ordered the man to bare his shoulder and stand straight while he pierced the shoulder through with a spear.

sentences.zh: 於耀靈殿上養驢數十頭，所自乘馬，養於御牀側。

translations.literal: In the Hall of Radiant Spirits he kept dozens of donkeys; the horse he rode himself was kept at the side of the imperial couch.
translations.idiomatic: In the Hall of Radiant Spirits he kept dozens of donkeys; the horse he rode himself was kept at the side of the imperial couch.

sentences.zh: 先是民間訛言，謂太宗不男，陳太妃本李道兒妾，道路之言，或云道兒子也。

translations.literal: Before this folk rumor said Taizong was not a man; the grand imperial consort had originally been a concubine of Li Dao'er, and according to talk on the roads some said Yu was Li Dao'er's son.
translations.idiomatic: Before this folk rumor said Taizong was not a man; the grand imperial consort had originally been a concubine of Li Dao'er, and according to talk on the roads some said Yu was Li Dao'er's son.

sentences.zh: 昱每出入去來，常自稱劉統，或自號李將軍。

translations.literal: Whenever Yu went out or came in he constantly called himself Liu Tong, or styled himself General Li.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Yu went out or came in he constantly called himself Liu Tong, or styled himself General Li.

sentences.zh: 與右衞翼輦營女子私通，每從之遊，持數千錢，供酒肉之費。

translations.literal: He privately knew women of the Right Guard's Imperial Carriage Escort camp and often went with them on his excursions, carrying several thousand cash to supply the cost of wine and meat.
translations.idiomatic: He privately knew women of the Right Guard's Imperial Carriage Escort camp and often went with them on his excursions, carrying several thousand cash to pay for wine and meat.

sentences.zh: 阮佃夫腹心人張羊為佃夫所委信。

translations.literal: Zhang Yang, a confidant of Ruan Tianfu, was someone whom Ruan Tianfu had entrusted and trusted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yang, a confidant of Ruan Tianfu, was someone Ruan Tianfu had entrusted and trusted.

sentences.zh: 佃夫敗，叛走，後捕得，昱自於承明門以車轢殺之。

translations.literal: When Ruan Tianfu was defeated Zhang Yang fled in rebellion; later when captured, Yu himself at the Chenming Gate had him crushed to death with a cart wheel.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruan Tianfu was defeated Zhang Yang fled in rebellion; later when captured, Yu himself at the Chenming Gate had him crushed to death beneath a cart wheel.

sentences.zh: 杜延載、沈勃、杜幼文、孫超，皆躬運矛鋋，手自臠割。

translations.literal: Du Yanzai, Shen Bo, Du Youwen, and Sun Chao — he all personally wielded spear and trident and with his own hands performed the dismemberment.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yanzai, Shen Bo, Du Youwen, and Sun Chao — for all of them he personally wielded spear and trident and with his own hands performed the dismemberment.

sentences.zh: 執幼文兄叔文於玄武湖北，昱馳馬執矟，自往刺之。

translations.literal: He seized Du Youwen's elder brother Shuwən at the north of Xuánwǔ Lake; Yu galloped on horseback grasping a spear and went himself to stab him.
translations.idiomatic: He seized Du Youwen's elder brother Shuwen at the north of Xuanwu Lake; Yu galloped on horseback grasping a spear and went himself to stab him.

sentences.zh: 制露車一乘，其上施篷，乘以出入，從者不過數十人。

translations.literal: He had made an open carriage with an awning mounted upon it for going in and out; his followers numbered no more than several dozen.
translations.idiomatic: He had made an open carriage with an awning mounted upon it for going in and out; his followers numbered no more than several dozen.

sentences.zh: 羽儀追之恒不及；

translations.literal: The honor guard pursuing him constantly could not catch up;
translations.idiomatic: The honor guard pursuing him constantly could not catch up;

sentences.zh: 又各慮禍，亦不敢追尋，唯整部伍，別在一處瞻望而已。

translations.literal: moreover each feared disaster and did not dare pursue — they only kept the unit in formation at a separate place to watch from afar.
translations.idiomatic: moreover each feared disaster and did not dare pursue — they only kept the unit in formation at a separate place to watch from afar.

sentences.zh: 凡諸鄙事，過目則能，鍛鍊金銀，裁衣作帽，莫不精絕。

translations.literal: In all vulgar crafts whatever caught his eye he could do; forging and refining gold and silver, cutting clothes and making caps — nothing was not consummately skilled.
translations.idiomatic: In all vulgar crafts whatever caught his eye he could do; forging and refining gold and silver, cutting clothes and making caps — nothing was not consummately skilled.

sentences.zh: 未嘗吹篪，執管便韻。

translations.literal: He had never played the vertical flute, yet taking the pipe in hand the tones were true.
translations.idiomatic: He had never played the vertical flute, yet taking the pipe in hand the tones were true.

sentences.zh: 天性好殺，以此為歡，一日無事，輒慘慘不樂。

translations.literal: By nature he loved killing, and made this his pleasure; when one day was without affair he was constantly despondent and unhappy.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he loved killing and made this his pleasure; when a day passed without such business he was constantly despondent and unhappy.

sentences.zh: 內外百司，人不自保，殿省憂遑，夕不及旦。

translations.literal: Within and without, the hundred offices — no man could keep himself safe; the palace and government dwelt in dread, evening not reaching dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Within and without the hundred offices, no man could keep himself safe; the palace and government dwelt in dread from evening until dawn.

sentences.zh: 齊王順天人之心，潛圖廢立，與直閤將軍王敬則謀之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi conformed to the hearts of Heaven and men, plotting in secret a deposition and enthronement, and took counsel with Wang Jingze, General of Direct Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qi conformed to the hearts of Heaven and men, plotting in secret a deposition and enthronement, and took counsel with Wang Jingze, General of Direct Attendants.

sentences.zh: 七月七日，昱乘露車，從二百許人，無復鹵簿羽儀，往青園尼寺，晚至新安寺就曇度道人飲酒。

translations.literal: On the seventh day of the seventh month Yu rode the open carriage with some two hundred men, no longer with the full guard of honor; he went to the Green Garden Nunnery, and in the evening arrived at Xin'an Temple to drink wine with the monk Tandu.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventh day of the seventh month Yu rode the open carriage with some two hundred men, no longer with the full guard of honor; he went to the Green Garden Nunnery, and in the evening arrived at Xin'an Temple to drink wine with the monk Tandu.

sentences.zh: 醉，夕扶還於仁壽殿東阿氈幄中臥。

translations.literal: Drunk, in the evening he was helped back to lie in the wool canopy on the east side of the Hall of Benevolent Longevity.
translations.idiomatic: Drunk, in the evening he was helped back to lie in the wool canopy on the east side of the Hall of Benevolent Longevity.

sentences.zh: 時昱出入無恒，省內諸閤，夜皆不閉。

translations.literal: At the time Yu's comings and goings had no fixed pattern; the various inner gate chambers at night were all left unclosed.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Yu's comings and goings had no fixed pattern; the various inner gate chambers at night were all left unclosed.

sentences.zh: 且羣下畏相逢值，無敢出者。

translations.literal: Moreover the crowd below feared meeting him; none dared come out.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the crowd below feared meeting him; none dared come out.

sentences.zh: 宿衞並逃避，內外無相禁攝。

translations.literal: The night guard all fled; inwardly and outwardly there was none to restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: The night guard all fled; inwardly and outwardly there was none to restrain him.

sentences.zh: 王敬則先結昱左右楊玉夫、楊萬年、呂欣之、湯成之、陳奉伯、張石留、羅僧智、鍾千載、嚴道福、雷道賜、戴昭祖、許啟、戚元寶、盛道泰、鍾千秋、王天寶、公上延孫、俞成、錢道寶、馬敬之、陳寶直、吳璩之、劉印魯、唐天寶、俞孫等二十五人，謀共取昱。

translations.literal: Wang Jingze had first won over Yu's attendants Yang Yufu, Yang Wannian, Lü Xinzi, Tang Chengzi, Chen Fengbo, Zhang Shiliu, Luo Sengzhi, Zhong Qianzai, Yan Daofu, Lei Daoci, Dai Zhaozu, Xu Qi, Qi Yuanyao, Sheng Daotai, Zhong Qianqiu, Wang Tianbao, Gong Shangyansun, Yu Cheng, Qian Daobao, Ma Jingzhi, Chen Baozhi, Wu Xu, Liu Yinlu, Tang Tianbao, Yu Sun, and twenty-five others besides, plotting together to seize Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jingze had first won over Yu's attendants Yang Yufu, Yang Wannian, Lü Xinzi, Tang Chengzi, Chen Fengbo, Zhang Shiliu, Luo Sengzhi, Zhong Qianzai, Yan Daofu, Lei Daoci, Dai Zhaozu, Xu Qi, Qi Yuanyao, Sheng Daotai, Zhong Qianqiu, Wang Tianbao, Gong Shangyansun, Yu Cheng, Qian Daobao, Ma Jingzhi, Chen Baozhi, Wu Xu, Liu Yinlu, Tang Tianbao, Yu Sun, and twenty-five others besides, plotting together to seize Yu.

sentences.zh: 其夕，敬則出外，玉夫見昱醉熟無所知，乃與萬年同入氈幄內，以昱防身刀斬之。

translations.literal: That evening Jingze went out; Yufu saw Yu drunk and deep asleep with no awareness, and together with Wannian entered the wool canopy and with Yu's personal defense knife cut him down.
translations.idiomatic: That evening Jingze went out; Yufu saw Yu drunk and deep asleep with no awareness, and together with Wannian entered the wool canopy and with Yu's personal defense knife cut him down.

sentences.zh: 奉伯提昱首，依常行法，稱敕開承明門出，以首與敬則，馳至領軍府，以首呈齊王。

translations.literal: Fengbo took Yu's head and, following the usual routine under imperial command, had the Chenming Gate opened and went out, giving the head to Jingze; he raced to the Commandant's headquarters and presented the head to the Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Fengbo took Yu's head and, following the usual routine under imperial command, had the Chenming Gate opened and went out, giving the head to Jingze; he raced to the Commandant's headquarters and presented the head to the Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 王乃戎服，率左右數十人，稱行還，開承明門入。

translations.literal: The prince then donned military dress, led several dozen men to his left and right, announced that he was returning on patrol, and entered through the Chenming Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The prince then donned military dress, led several dozen men to his left and right, announced that he was returning on patrol, and entered through the Chenming Gate.

sentences.zh: 昱他夕每開門，門者震懾不敢視，至是弗之疑。

translations.literal: On other nights whenever Yu opened the gate the gatekeepers were shaken with fear and did not dare look up; this time they did not suspect him.
translations.idiomatic: On other nights whenever Yu opened the gate the gatekeepers were shaken with fear and did not dare look up; this time they did not suspect him.

sentences.zh: 齊王既入，曉，乃奉太后令奉迎安成王。

translations.literal: Once the Prince of Qi had entered, at dawn he then presented the empress dowager's order to welcome the Prince of Ancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Prince of Qi had entered, at dawn he then presented the empress dowager's order to welcome the Prince of Ancheng.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：喪國亡家之主，雖適末同途，發軫或異也。

translations.literal: The historian says: Lords who lose their states and ruin their families — though they reach the end by the same road, the point at which they set out may differ.
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: Lords who lose their states and ruin their families — though they reach the end by the same road, the point at which they set out may differ.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝卑遊褻幸，皆龍駕帝飾，傳警清路；

translations.literal: The Former Deposed Emperor debased himself in wandering and lewd favor, yet all were with imperial carriage and emblems, with mounted outriders clearing the road;
translations.idiomatic: The Former Deposed Emperor debased himself in wandering and lewd favor, yet all were with imperial carriage and emblems, with mounted outriders clearing the road;

sentences.zh: 蒼梧王則藏璽懷紱，魚服忘反，危冠短服，匹馬孤征。

translations.literal: the Prince of Cangwu hid the seal and kept the tasseled cord in his bosom, fish-robes forgotten in return, perilous caps and short dress, a single horse riding alone.
translations.idiomatic: the Prince of Cangwu hid the seal and kept the tasseled cord in his bosom, fish-robes forgotten in return, perilous caps and short dress, a single horse riding alone.

sentences.zh: 至於殞身覆祚，其理若一。

translations.literal: As for the ruin of body and the overturning of the throne, the principle is as one.
translations.idiomatic: As for the ruin of body and the overturning of the throne, the principle is as one.

sentences.zh: 姬、夏之隆，質文異尚，亡國之道，其亦然乎。

translations.literal: The grandeur of Ji and Xia — substance and pattern differently esteemed — the way of a lost state: is it likewise?
translations.idiomatic: The grandeur of Ji and Xia — substance and pattern differently esteemed — the way of a lost state: is it likewise?

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Textual collation notes

sentences.zh: 冬十月辛卯 下有辛未。

translations.literal: Under "winter, tenth month xinmao" there is xinwei below.
translations.idiomatic: Under "winter, tenth month xinmao" there is xinwei below.

sentences.zh: 按是月庚戌朔，二十二日辛未，無辛卯。

translations.literal: According to this month, new moon on gengxu, the twenty-second day is xinwei; there is no xinmao.
translations.idiomatic: According to this month, new moon on gengxu, the twenty-second day is xinwei; there is no xinmao.

sentences.zh: 以越州刺史陳伯紹為交州刺史 張森楷校勘記云：「按明帝紀，泰始五年，伯紹為交州刺史。

translations.literal: "Inspector of Yue Chen Bozhao made Inspector of Jiao" — Zhang Senkai's collation notes say: "According to the annals of Emperor Ming, in the fifth year of Taishi Bozhao was Inspector of Jiao.
translations.idiomatic: "Inspector of Yue Chen Bozhao made Inspector of Jiao" — Zhang Senkai's collation notes say: "According to the annals of Emperor Ming, in the fifth year of Taishi Bozhao was Inspector of Jiao.

sentences.zh: 七年，置越州。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Yue Province was established.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Yue Province was established.

sentences.zh: 南齊書州郡志云，元徽二年，陳伯紹為越州刺史，當即指此。

translations.literal: The Treatise on Provinces and Commanderies in the Book of Southern Qi says that in the second year of Yuanhui Chen Bozhao was Inspector of Yue Province — this must refer to this passage.
translations.idiomatic: The Treatise on Provinces and Commanderies in the Book of Southern Qi says that in the second year of Yuanhui Chen Bozhao was Inspector of Yue Province — this must refer to this passage.

sentences.zh: 此當是以交州刺史陳伯紹為越州刺史，刻譌互倒。」

translations.literal: Here it should read that Inspector of Jiao Chen Bozhao was made Inspector of Yue Province — the characters were transposed in carving."
translations.idiomatic: Here it should read that Inspector of Jiao Chen Bozhao was made Inspector of Yue Province — the characters were transposed in carving."

sentences.zh: 五月壬午「壬午」各本並作「壬子」，據南史、建康實錄、通鑑改。

translations.literal: Fifth month renwu: in all editions "renwu" reads "renzi"; changed according to the History of the Southern Dynasties, Veritable Record of Jiankang, and Comprehensive Mirror.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month renwu: in all editions "renwu" reads "renzi"; changed according to the History of the Southern Dynasties, Veritable Record of Jiankang, and Comprehensive Mirror.

sentences.zh: 按是月辛未朔，十三日壬午，無壬子。

translations.literal: According to this month, new moon on xinwei, the thirteenth day is renwu; there is no renzi.
translations.idiomatic: According to this month, new moon on xinwei, the thirteenth day is renwu; there is no renzi.

sentences.zh: 賊黨杜黑蠡丁文豪分軍向朱雀航「杜黑蠡」魏書作「杜黑騾」。

translations.literal: The rebel band Du Heili and Ding Wenhao divided their forces toward the Zhuque floating bridge: "Du Heili" in the Book of Wei reads "Du Heilü."
translations.idiomatic: The rebel band Du Heili and Ding Wenhao divided their forces toward the Zhuque floating bridge: "Du Heili" in the Book of Wei reads "Du Heilü."

sentences.zh: 甲午 各本並作「戊午」，據局本及南史、建康實錄改。

translations.literal: jiawu: in all editions it reads "wuwu"; changed according to the Bureau edition, the History of the Southern Dynasties, and the Veritable Record of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: jiawu: in all editions it reads "wuwu"; changed according to the Bureau edition, the History of the Southern Dynasties, and the Veritable Record of Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 是月辛未朔，二十四日甲午，無戊午。

translations.literal: According to this month, new moon on xinwei, the twenty-fourth day is jiawu; there is no wuwu.
translations.idiomatic: According to this month, new moon on xinwei, the twenty-fourth day is jiawu; there is no wuwu.

sentences.zh: 撫軍典籤茅恬開東府納賊「撫軍」南史作「車騎」，建康實錄作「護軍」。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk of the Army Who Pacifies Mao Tian opened the Eastern Palace to admit rebels: "Army Who Pacifies" in the History of the Southern Dynasties reads "General of Chariots and Cavalry," and in the Veritable Record of Jiankang reads "General Who Guards the Army."
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk of the Army Who Pacifies Mao Tian opened the Eastern Palace to admit rebels: "Army Who Pacifies" in the History of the Southern Dynasties reads "General of Chariots and Cavalry," and in the Veritable Record of Jiankang reads "General Who Guards the Army."

sentences.zh: 鎮北將軍南徐州刺史建平王景素進號征北將軍 各本並脫「南」字，據景素傳補。

translations.literal: General Who Guards the North and Inspector of Southern Xu Province, the Prince of Jianping Jing Su, was advanced in title to General Who Campaigns in the North: in all editions the character "South" is missing and is supplied according to the biography of Jing Su.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Guards the North and Inspector of Southern Xu Province, the Prince of Jianping Jing Su, was promoted to General Who Campaigns in the North: in all editions the character "South" is missing and is supplied according to the biography of Jing Su.

sentences.zh: 穀人五斛 各本並脫「人」字，據元龜二０七補。

translations.literal: five hu of grain per person: in all editions the character "person" is missing and is supplied according to Yuan gui 207.
translations.idiomatic: five hu of grain per person: in all editions the character "person" is missing and is supplied according to Yuan gui 207.

sentences.zh: 八月庚子 按是月癸亥朔，無庚子，初三日庚午，庚子或是庚午之譌。

translations.literal: Eighth month gengzi: according to this month, new moon on guihai, there is no gengzi; the third day is gengwu — gengzi may be a corruption for gengwu.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month gengzi: according to this month, new moon on guihai, there is no gengzi; the third day is gengwu — gengzi may be a corruption for gengwu.

sentences.zh: 而國度弘費「弘」各本並作「引」，據元龜四七一改。

translations.literal: "Yet state expenditures are vast" — "vast" in all editions reads "draw"; changed according to Yuan gui 471.
translations.idiomatic: "Yet state expenditures are vast" — "vast" in all editions reads "draw"; changed according to Yuan gui 471.

sentences.zh: 則氓隸齊歡「隸」各本並作「祇」，據元龜四七一改。

translations.literal: "Then commoners and servants alike would rejoice" — "servants" in all editions reads "spirit"; changed according to Yuan gui 471.
translations.idiomatic: "Then commoners and servants alike would rejoice" — "servants" in all editions reads "spirit"; changed according to Yuan gui 471.

sentences.zh: 驍騎將軍全景文為南豫州刺史「驍騎」各本並作「驃騎」，據南齊書呂安國傳全景文附傳改。

translations.literal: Quan Jingwen, General of Valiant Cavalry, made Inspector of Southern Yu Province: "Valiant Cavalry" in all editions reads "Agile Cavalry"; changed according to the attached biography of Quan Jingwen in the biography of Lü Anguo in the Book of Southern Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Jingwen, General of Valiant Cavalry, appointed Inspector of Southern Yu Province: "Valiant Cavalry" in all editions reads "Agile Cavalry"; changed according to the attached biography of Quan Jingwen in the biography of Lü Anguo in the Book of Southern Qi.
